name: Ratatui
vendor: The Ratatui Developers (forked from tui-rs by Florian Dehau)
summary: A Rust library for terminal user interfaces that redraws the whole screen from your app’s state on every frame, then writes only the cells that changed.
intro: Ratatui draws in immediate mode. Your program owns its state and its loop; each time it wants to update the screen it calls `terminal.draw()` with a closure, and inside that closure it renders every widget again into a `Buffer`, a grid of `Cell`s that each hold one symbol and its style. Widgets are plain values that implement a `render()` method and are thrown away after the frame. When the closure returns, Ratatui compares the new buffer with the previous one and writes only the difference to the terminal, then swaps the two buffers. Layout is computed from constraints such as `Length(3)` or `Fill(1)` that split a `Rect` into smaller areas.

Ratatui only renders. Reading keys and mouse events, raw mode and the alternate screen come from a backend library: Crossterm by default, or Termion, Termwiz or Termina, plus a `TestBackend` for unit tests. Since version 0.30 (December 2025) the project is a workspace of crates: `ratatui-core` holds the traits and types and changes slowly, so third-party widget crates can depend on it, while `ratatui-widgets` and one crate per backend sit on top. With default features off, it compiles for `no_std` targets; the team reports running it on ESP32 and STM32H7 microcontrollers.

The project is a community fork of tui-rs, which Florian Dehau wrote in 2016 and stopped maintaining. Ratatui’s first release, 0.20.0, came out in March 2023, and tui-rs now points its users to it. It is still released as 0.x and is actively developed: 0.30.2 shipped in June 2026, and commits landed in October 2026. OpenAI’s Codex CLI draws its terminal interface with it.
strengths: No widget tree to keep in sync: the UI is a function of your state, which sidesteps most of the lifetime and ownership fights a retained widget tree causes in Rust
Double buffering with a diff means each frame writes only changed cells to the terminal, however much the app redraws
Does not take over your program: there is no `app.run()` event loop, so it can be added to an existing program, even just to chart its internal state
Pluggable backends (Crossterm, Termion, Termwiz, Termina) and `no_std` support reach from desktop terminals to microcontrollers, and `TestBackend` lets you unit test the UI without a terminal
limits: Still 0.x: minor releases carry breaking changes (0.30 removed `block::Title`, renamed `Alignment` and changed the `Backend` trait), listed in a separate BREAKING-CHANGES.md
You write the event loop, input handling and app structure yourself; if the loop blocks, the screen stops updating
Widgets keep nothing between frames, so a selection or scroll offset lives in a separate state value (such as `ListState` for a `StatefulWidget`) that your app stores and passes in each time
Needs a recent compiler: the minimum supported Rust version is 1.88 as of 0.30.1

source: // run() enters raw mode and the alternate screen, and restores them on exit
// Called for every frame: describe the whole screen from the current state.
frame.render_widget(Paragraph::new("Right arrow adds 10%, q quits"), rest);

story: Florian Dehau started tui-rs in 2016 as a Rust library for terminal dashboards, inspired by the JavaScript library blessed-contrib and the Go library termui. It rendered in immediate mode with intermediate buffers and left input handling to libraries such as Crossterm and Termion, and its popularity kept growing as people used it in more ambitious projects.

In August 2022 Dehau wrote that their work left little energy for the crate and asked for people to take it over, listing its gaps: complex layouts, scrolling and mouse support were hard, and it only suited full-screen apps. Contributors started a community fork in early 2023, moved the open pull requests over and released it as Ratatui 0.20.0 in March 2023, a maintenance release with bug fixes and no big features. In August 2023 tui-rs was marked unmaintained and its README pointed to Ratatui.

The fork kept the immediate-mode design and grew around it: a website with tutorials and templates, convenience functions such as `ratatui::init()` (0.28.1) and `ratatui::run()` (0.30), and in December 2025 a split into a workspace of crates with `no_std` support for embedded targets.

choices.why: Rebuilding widgets from state each frame avoids the lifetime and ownership problems that retained widget trees cause in Rust, which Dehau saw as one reason beginners liked the crate; the buffer diff keeps the terminal output small.

tui-rs never had an `app.run()` that takes over execution, so it could be dropped into any program, even just to visualize a program’s internal state. Ratatui kept that: input comes from the backend, and the loop is yours.

The original maintainer had stepped back and changes were waiting unreleased. A community fork under a new name let new maintainers transfer the open pull requests from tui-rs and ship them, starting with a fixes-only release.

choices.choice: Split into a workspace of crates in 0.30
choices.why: A slower-moving `ratatui-core` gives widget authors a more stable API, and separate widget and backend crates cut compile times and let apps pick their dependencies.

timeline.text: Dehau asks the community to take over maintenance (August)
Community fork released as Ratatui 0.20.0 (March); tui-rs marked unmaintained (August)
Ratatui 0.30 splits into crates and adds `no_std` support (December)
